subject: Clarification on cross-border SCC module selection for Clearpath Health
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@clearpathhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SCC module guidance request (EU/UK) — Clearpath Health

Hi Tessa,

Hope you're well. We're finalizing our DPA and need to confirm which 2021 SCC module(s) you recommend for transfers from our EU entities to Redwood. A few constraints to keep in mind:

- Clearpath is a US-based data processor for certain analytics but acts as a controller for patient records; the flow in-scope will be EU patient data (healthcare) going to Redwood for inference and model hosting (so Redwood would be a processor).
- We also must satisfy UK transfer requirements and will need an addendum if applicable.
- We have HIPAA obligations internally and need to make sure there aren't conflicts between the SCCs selection and a potential BAA/contract language.

Can you confirm which module(s) you use for controller -> processor relationships and whether Redwood recommends an explicit UK addendum for this use case? If helpful, please attach the latest DPA/SCC template.

Thank you — this is on our procurement path and the legal team has a short turnaround.

Best,
Anna
Anna Lopez
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Clearpath Health

Attachments: none
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2024 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCC module guidance request (EU/UK) — Clearpath Health

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: for EU -> Redwood (controller -> processor) we typically adopt the 2021 SCCs Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) and we apply the analogous UK addendum for UK-origin data. That approach aligns with most of our healthcare customers who are controllers.

Two quick notes:
- If Clearpath will also act as a processor for any downstream flows (e.g., passing data to another processor), we can map those as Processor-to-Processor (Module Four) where relevant; we can highlight those segments in the contract.
- On HIPAA: the SCCs selection doesn't change Redwood's willingness to sign a BAA (we have a separate BAA process). We should scope the data categories and processing activities in the DPA/BAA so there's no ambiguity.

I've looped in our legal and privacy leads to confirm the final language and to attach the DPA + SCCs template for your review.

Next steps: I'll have legal confirm the recommended language and circulate the editable SCCs module selection worksheet. Are you under a timing constraint this week?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2024 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SCC module guidance request (EU/UK) — Clearpath Health

Laura / Markus / Vivek — forwarding Clearpath's note (below). Key asks: they need explicit confirmation of the SCC module(s) for their EU -> US transfers and an acknowledgement about the UK addendum. They also flagged HIPAA and want to confirm there are no conflicts if we also execute a BAA.

Could you:
- Confirm we recommend Module Two (controller -> processor) for both EU and UK with the UK addendum included, and whether we should also mark any subprocessors as Module Four segments in the worksheet.
- Review our latest DPA (I attached v3.4) and confirm if any HIPAA-specific clauses need to be surfaced before we share with the customer.
- Produce the SCCs selection worksheet (docx) and UK addendum template for signature.

Timeline: procurement is asking for contract language this week; they indicated a 72-hour SLA after we send the templates.

Quote from Anna's original: "We have HIPAA obligations internally and need to make sure there aren't conflicts between the SCCs selection and a potential BAA/contract language."

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Tessa

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.4.pdf
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2024 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SCC module guidance request (EU/UK) — Clearpath Health

Tessa / team — reviewed. Recommendation and deliverables below.

Recommendation:
- Primary: Adopt Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) for the EU transfers and apply the UK Addendum for UK-origin data. This is the standard and clearest mapping for a customer controller sending data to Redwood as processor.
- Subprocessors: Where Redwood engages subprocessors, we will run Processor-to-Processor (Module Four) language in the mapping appendix; we will not change the principal Module Two mapping for the main flow.
- HIPAA: No conflict between SCCs Module Two + UK addendum and a BAA. The DPA should explicitly reference the BAA as an ancillary agreement that governs PHI obligations; we suggest a short cross-reference clause. If Clearpath requires Redwood to sign a full HIPAA BAA (rather than a cross-reference), we can accommodate but will need legal approval on a per-customer basis.

Deliverables attached for sharing with Clearpath:
- Redwood_DPA_v3.4.pdf (clean copy)
- SCCs-Module-Selection-Clearpath-CPH-119.docx (selection worksheet with Module Two pre-filled and subprocessors noted)
- UK-Addendum-signed-template.pdf (standard UK addendum to 2021 SCCs)

Action items for Sales (Tessa):
1) Share the three attachments with Clearpath procurement and legal.
2) Ask Clearpath whether they want a BAA signature now or prefer an initial cross-reference with a follow-up BAA. If they want immediate BAA execution, route to Legal for a BAA engagement (I can lead).
3) Confirm the list of EU entities and any downstream recipients that might require Module Four mapping.

I'll be available to join a call with Clearpath legal if they'd like to walk through the worksheet.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
